title: Loop+ Membership Cancellation and Resumption
content:
Loop+ Membership Terms — cancellation.

**Cancelling is the buyer's own decision and is confirmed by the buyer. By default a cancellation turns off renewal and the membership ends on the paid-through date, or on the trial end date during a trial, with benefits until then. Until that date the buyer may resume, returning to trial or active as before with no new charge.**

A default cancellation does not end the membership on the day it is made. It turns off renewal (on a paid membership, auto-renew; during a trial, the conversion to a paid membership), and the membership is then pending cancellation, with the date it will end recorded as its cancellation effective date. When that date is reached the membership is cancelled.

| Status when the buyer cancels | Date the membership ends | Benefits | If the buyer resumes before that date |
|---|---|---|---|
| Active (paid) | the paid-through date | continue until the paid-through date | returns to active, with no new charge |
| Trial | the trial end date | continue until the trial end date | returns to trial, with no new charge; the cancellation effective date is cleared |

Points of judgement:

- **Who decides.** The cancellation is the buyer's decision, and the buyer confirms it.
- **What changes at once.** Only renewal is turned off; benefits remain until the paid-through date or the trial end date.
- **Resuming.** Until the date the membership is due to end, the buyer may resume. A resumed membership goes back to the status it had — trial or active — and no new charge is made.

Hypothetical case: a buyer on a paid plan whose paid-through date is 31 August cancels on 12 August. Renewal is turned off, benefits continue to 31 August and the membership ends on that date. If the buyer resumes on 20 August, the membership is active again with no new charge.
